name: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF): India's 2027 Blending Mandate
scope: India notified SAF blending in ATF regulations (Apr 2026) and mandated a 1% SAF blend from Jan 2027 (2% 2028, 5% 2030 proposed); refiners are co-processing used cooking oil (UCO) and building ethanol-to-jet capacity, with Praj supplying technology. Listed exposure is mostly PSU large caps plus Praj (mid cap, de-rated ~-38% in 6 months); no small cap confirmed; SAF costs 3-5x jet fuel and depends on a pending subsidy/fixed-price model, so it is early on policy detail but not an undiscovered small-cap play.
questions: What exactly is SAF, which pathways matter for India (UCO co-processing/HEFA, ethanol/alcohol-to-jet, other) and what feedstock rules does the draft SAF policy set (food crops barred, molasses allowed)?

What is the current mandate and timeline (1% from Jan 2027 for international flights, 2% 2028, 5% 2030, draft 40% by 2040), what is the status of the fixed-price/subsidy model, and what is the CORSIA link?
What is India's likely SAF demand in 2027-2030 versus certified supply, and is co-processing capacity enough for 2027?

What are Indian Oil (Panipat co-processing and ethanol-to-jet with LanzaJet, Paradip UCO JV approved May 2026), BPCL (Mumbai ISCC CORSIA certification, unit expected end-2026), HPCL (Visakh demo plant, ~10 TMT/yr from Jan 2027) and MRPL (UCO tender May 2026) actually doing, with volumes, capex and dates?
What is Praj Industries' role (IOC JV, IATA/ISMA certification MoU, ethanol-to-SAF engineering order from an international customer in Q1 FY27) and how much of its order book is SAF?

Does NTPC's reported ethanol-to-SAF plant (EPC to GPS Renewables) and any other listed participant (sugar/distillery companies, UCO collectors/biodiesel makers, the unnamed Paradip JV partner) clear the evidence bar?
Is any small cap genuinely involved (UCO aggregation, biodiesel, ethanol-to-jet feedstock) or is exposure limited to large PSUs and Praj?
How material is SAF to each company's earnings (margin pressure for refiners if subsidy is not paid versus upside for technology/EPC suppliers)?
Has the market already priced this in: stock performance over 6-12 months (Praj down ~38% in 6 months to early Nov 2026) and the extent of broker/media 'SAF stocks' coverage?
What are the key risks and catalysts: final SAF policy and pricing, UCO feedstock supply, CORSIA certification, first commercial volumes in Jan 2027, Praj order wins?

refiners_saf_producers: PSU refiners co-processing UCO and building SAF/ethanol-to-jet capacity to meet the mandate
technology_engineering: Process technology and plant suppliers for ethanol-to-SAF and biofuel plants
